empirical_precedent: 18 blind participants completed three months of tactile training; seven reported visual-like qualia and that subgroup showed occipital EEG recruitment
what_it_supports: Repeated nonvisual input can be learned and can be associated with changed perceptual experience and neural recruitment in a heterogeneous blind sample
what_it_does_not_support: An effect of language-only AI descriptions; a universal effect; or long-term AI neuroplasticity

empirical_precedent: Six-month visual-to-tactile substitution training in blind children reported greater somatosensory-thalamic to occipital functional connectivity associated with tactile performance
what_it_supports: Training-related functional reorganization is biologically plausible under a prolonged tactile intervention
what_it_does_not_support: Any immediate dream effect; an AI effect; or a result generalizable to blind adults

empirical_precedent: Congenitally blind adults learned letter soundscapes; VWFA selectivity was reported, with one novel-script effect after less than two hours
what_it_supports: Nonvisual encodings can support learned task-specific representations
what_it_does_not_support: That ordinary natural-language descriptions recruit the same mechanism or alter dreams

empirical_precedent: BLV art-exploration participants described detailed spatial and contextual information as useful for forming a mental model; preferences were heterogeneous
what_it_supports: Accessible descriptions can be material from which some BLV users construct an internal spatial/contextual understanding
what_it_does_not_support: A neural change, dream incorporation, or a preference shared by all BLV users

empirical_precedent: Interview study of 14 visually impaired people using LMM assistance describes translation of visual surroundings to language alongside hallucination, social-context, and intent failures
what_it_supports: Assistive AI can function as a repeated visual-to-language information channel and has agency/reliability risks
what_it_does_not_support: Dream incorporation, causal cognitive change, or the prevalence of any failure mode

empirical_precedent: A sleep-laboratory study found that blinded raters could sometimes identify a presleep audiobook from dream reports; all-rater agreement on direct or indirect audiobook incorporation occurred in 7 cases (11% of reports)
what_it_supports: Narrative information immediately before sleep can sometimes be detected in later dream reports; blinded source-assignment coding is feasible
what_it_does_not_support: An AI-specific effect; an effect in blind participants; a high or inevitable incorporation rate; or causality beyond the experimental narrative exposure

empirical_precedent: Meta-analysis of 16 studies/45 effects reported an association between learning-related dreams and post-sleep memory performance
what_it_supports: Dream incorporation has a documented relationship with learning/memory outcomes
what_it_does_not_support: That dream incorporation causes consolidation or that any particular pre-sleep content will appear in dreams
